targets._note: Real Census 2021 / ASHE 2024 figures pulled via Nomis API and ONS downloads (see sources, provenance/). age = % adults 18+; eth = % all residents; act = % of 16+ (retired/other inactive 'other' folded into ho); ten = % households; 'inner' = 14 Inner London boroughs aggregate (E09000001,07,12,13,14,19,20,22,23,25,28,30,32,33).

unverified: Education by AGE (no Nomis 2021 table found): age shape is my prior, rescaled so the 16+ total matches TS067.
Birthplace COUNTRIES within each ethnic group (no table reached): hand lists; only the UK-born share is census-fitted at group level.
Religion and UK-born splits between sub-groups of Asian/Black/White Other: priors fitted (IPF) to the group totals only.
Health 5-category shape and by-age split inside 16-49 / 65+: prior shape rescaled to RM043 good/not-good totals.
Self-employment propensity by occupation, degree requirement by occupation, student-job occupation mix: my assumptions (ASHE covers employees only).
Tenure by age of reference person modifiers (tenAge): no 2021 table found; plausibility-checked only.
Men's childlessness (F table + offsets) and men's parity: assumption. 'Living apart together' share (lat): assumption.
Zero-hours/fixed-term/agency shares (contract): approximate LFS figures from memory; pattern multipliers (zh) are assumptions.
Shift patterns (days, start times, lengths) are modelling choices informed by common practice, not a dataset.
Household type split between multigen/shared/withparents from RM057's coarse categories: allocation fractions are assumptions.

inc ranges: lower/upper bounds follow the verified 2024/25 rates, but where people land inside the range (top-ups, housing element excluded, pension size above the State Pension, loan means-test minimum) is my assumption.

Home/family carers are down-weighted for unrelated sharers (x0.15) and people living alone (x0.35): Census activity tables are not available by household type, so the factors are reasoned (carers are mostly partnered parents), not fitted.
derived: act: 65+ row split into 65-74/75+ using prior shape; 18-24 student share assumes 90% of 16-17s are students; 'other' economically inactive folded into long-term sick / home carer pro rata.
